title: The Strike Notice
intro: You posted a photo of your cat on Chirp. A message arrives from "Chirp Safety".
Tap anything that looks odd to sniff it closer. Pin what is suspicious, clear what is harmless.
When you are sure, decide what to do.

notify.text: Copyright claim on your photo. Appeal within 24 hours…

banner.text: New message request · you do not follow this account

screen.context: You posted a photo of your cat this morning.

msg.text: Copyright claim: your photo breaks our rules.
password and the code we text you

dmfirst.label: They messaged first
dmfirst.lens: A private message from an account you do not follow.
dmfirst.why: Real platforms send notices inside the app, not through DMs from strangers.

tick.label: Fake tick
tick.lens: The ✔ is typed into the name. Chirp's real verified badge sits after the handle, and there is none.
tick.why: Anyone can type a tick into a display name.

handle.label: New look-alike account
handle.lens: Joined 3 days ago, 7 followers. Chirp's real account is @chirp.
handle.why: Brand-new look-alike accounts are a classic impersonation sign.

link.label: Look-alike link
link.lens: This goes to chirp-appeal.support, not the real chirp.app.
link.why: Never log in through a link in a message. Open the app yourself and look at your notices.

login.label: Asks for password and code
login.lens: It wants your password and your texted code.
login.why: No real platform needs your password or code for an appeal.

deadline.label: Delete-in-24-hours threat
deadline.lens: Your account will be deleted in 24 hours.
deadline.why: A threat with a short deadline is a pressure trick.

strike.label: Copyright claim
strike.lens: A claim that your cat photo breaks the rules.
strike.why: The claim sounds serious, but it comes from an unknown account. The claim alone proves nothing.

logo.label: Shield logo
logo.why: Logos are easy to copy, so they prove nothing on their own.

actions.label: Open the Chirp app and check my notices

trap.title: Chirp · Appeal
trap.ask: Enter your password and the code we text you to appeal.

block_report.line: Blocked and reported. The fake account was removed before it reached other people.

verify.line: The app showed no claim and no warning on your account. Case cracked.

ignore.line: You stayed safe. But the account is still out there messaging other people.

go_ahead.line: The page copied your password and code. Within minutes the account was locked and used to message your friends.

what_if.go_ahead: Opening the app yourself would have shown no claim anywhere. Real notices live inside the app.
what_if.ignore: Reporting takes two taps and gets the fake account removed.
what_if.verify: Checking was smart. Blocking and reporting as well protects others.

golden_rule: Real platforms send notices inside the app. A DM that threatens deletion and asks for your password is a trap.

quick_check.q: An account you do not follow DMs that your account will be deleted unless you log in through a link. What do you do?

options.text: Log in quickly through the link
Reply and explain your cat photo
Open the app yourself to check, then block and report
Ask your friends if they got it

quick_check.explain: Real notices live inside the app. Never log in through a link a stranger sends.

hints.nudge: Start with who sent it. Do you know this account?

rows.v: None. The ✔ is typed into the name

rows.k: Does Chirp DM you about strikes?
rows.v: Never. Notices appear in the app

rows.k: Does it ask for your password or code?
